title: A Smaller Index, a Narrow Rally
deck: IHSG rose 5.82% to 5,344.406, third of 32 markets in IDX's table. Five stocks made 46% of the gain, a Rp66.8tn share transfer doubled reported turnover, and the best day for shares was a record low for the rupiah. On Friday IDX cut the index from 818 stocks to 522. Our caution last week was wrong for the week. We still would not chase it.
description: Indonesia weekly research for 9 to 13 November 2026. Audited IDX data, the 296 concentrated stocks that left IHSG, the ADRO share transfer behind the turnover jump, foreign buying in three stocks, a rebuild of IDX's index contributions, global markets and a check of last week's call.

sections.title: The week proved us wrong. The rally is still too narrow to chase.

blocks.text: IHSG rose 5.82% to 5,344.406, a gain of 293.977 points. Among the 32 indices in IDX's global table only Taiwan and Japan did better. A week ago we said we would not buy. Anyone who followed that advice missed the week, and we say so before anything else.

The rise was led from the top. Five stocks, BBRI, BBCA, ASII, TLKM and BMRI, added 135.36 points, 46.04% of the gain. Below them it was broad: 549 of 945 stocks rose more than 2%. Foreign investors bought a net Rp462.73bn across all stocks, the first week of net buying in the eight weeks this weekly has covered. Rp443.44bn of it came on Thursday.

We read the number with care. Reported turnover doubled because the controlling holder of Alamtri Resources (ADRO) and Adaro Andalan (AADI) moved its shares through the negotiated market for Rp66.81tn. On Friday IDX changed the index itself, dropping 296 stocks with highly concentrated ownership. And Thursday, the best day for shares, was the day the rupiah hit a record low.

Our view moves part of the way. The large banks that foreign investors bought no longer look like the weak point, and we say that plainly. On the index we stay cautious. We would turn neutral on a close above 5,488, which needs a further 2.69% rise, if foreigners buy four of the five largest stocks for two weeks running and the rupiah holds after Bank Indonesia meets on 17 and 18 November.

blocks.label: Checking last week's call
blocks.text: We set five signposts. One passed. IDX now takes concentrated stocks out between reviews: MKNT, the Rp32 stock that added 12.40 points last week, had no index shares from Monday, and 296 more names went on Friday. The bond test half passed. Bids at Tuesday's government bond auction rose 156.38% to Rp79.71tn, but the 11-year FR0111 cleared 12 basis points higher. The bank test failed, because it asked for two weeks of buying and BBRI had been sold the week before. This week foreign investors bought BBCA and BBRI. Our estimate for BMRI is a net sale of Rp7.90bn, too small to tell from zero. IHSG stayed below 5,488. The North Asian sell-off we feared went the other way, and Taiwan rose 10.01%.

sections.title: Two days did most of the work

blocks.label: Exhibit 01
blocks.title: Four up days out of five, the biggest on Thursday
blocks.note: Select a date to inspect the closing observation. Lines join daily closes and show no intraday highs or lows.

blocks.text: Monday rose 0.46% to 5,073.770 and Tuesday 1.02% to 5,125.726. Wednesday slipped 0.21%. Thursday was the big day, a rise of 2.66% to 5,250.895 that closed at the day's high. Friday touched 5,361.939, the week's high, and closed 1.78% up at 5,344.406. Thursday and Friday made 229.371 points, 78.02% of the week.
On Tuesday IDX also delisted 18 companies, among them Sri Rejeki Isman (SRIL). At their last prices they were worth Rp8.11tn together, and the count of listed stocks fell from 963 to 945.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 02. Breadth by number of stocks, recomputed from IDX's counts

blocks.text: By value the rise was wider still. Stocks worth Rp6,906tn rose, 76.84% of the value in IDX's chart. IDX again printed the percentages of the two falling groups in each other's place, in both bars, so every share here comes from the counts.

sections.title: IHSG lost 296 members, and two banks moved further past the 9% cap

blocks.text: On Wednesday evening, 11 November, IDX and KSEI published a new list of companies with highly concentrated ownership, judged mainly by the stake of the ten largest holders together with scrip shares. It named 383 companies, 40.53% of the 945 listed, and 300 of them were new. Under IDX's October rule such stocks leave IHSG between reviews instead of waiting for the next one. IDX confirmed the leavers on Thursday night, and on Friday 13 November 296 of the new names left. The other four were not index members.

blocks.label: Exhibit 03
blocks.title: The 296 leavers were 17% of market value but 6% of what IHSG counted
blocks.note: Ribbon width is market value at the 12 November close, in Rp tn. The counted part of the 522 grew to Rp1,738.25tn by Friday's close, which matches IDX's printed Rp1,738tn.

blocks.text: The departures sound large and were not. At Thursday's close the 296 stocks were worth Rp1,116.32tn, 17.04% of the full value of the index. IHSG counts only free float, though, and IDX counted Rp108.63tn of theirs, 5.98% of the counted total. Only 9.73% of their value was counted at all, against 31.43% for the stocks that stay. Our sums from IDX's stock data match the capitalisation IDX prints on its daily page 1 for both days.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 04. Largest IHSG weights before and after 13 November, from IDX's annex

blocks.text: Removing stocks does not move the level on the day, because IDX resets the divisor. It does change what the index measures. The larger remaining weights rose by about 6.4%. BBCA went from 9.75% to 10.38% and BBRI from 9.35% to 9.95%, both above the 9% cap that IDX's October rule keeps. The five largest stocks now make up 38.56% of IHSG, and three banks 28.15%.

The 296 rose 2.34% over the week on full value and the 522 rose 5.67%. The gap was widest on Thursday, the day after the list came out, at 0.64% against 2.69%. We have no figure for the money that tracks IHSG, so we cannot say how much of that gap was index selling.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: The rule measures concentration. IDX's notice says the list does not by itself indicate any violation, and it includes Pertamina Geothermal (PGEO), Garuda Indonesia (GIAA), Wijaya Karya (WIKA) and HM Sampoerna (HMSP). So does Saratoga (SRTG), one of the four companies that received ADRO shares on Tuesday. The new index carries more bank risk, and two banks that already sat above the 9% cap, BBCA at 9.75% and BBRI at 9.35%, now sit further above it. IDX has not said when it will apply the cap again. Funds that benchmark to IHSG need that answer before the January review.

sections.title: Turnover doubled on one share transfer

blocks.caption: Exhibit 05. Where the controlling stakes in ADRO and AADI went on 10 November, from the KSEI ownership reports

blocks.text: On Tuesday PT Adaro Strategic Investments moved its entire 48.768% stake in ADRO and its entire 41.0965% stake in AADI to the same four companies through the negotiated market. ADRO's filing says control did not change and the business is not affected. AADI filed a notice under the same heading that afternoon, and the buyers' reports to KSEI price the AADI shares at Rp10,286. IDX's stock summary puts the negotiated trades at Rp33.89tn in ADRO and Rp32.92tn in AADI, 88.33% of all value traded that day. Kontan reports the same two figures.

Take those two trades out and the week's value averaged Rp10.34tn a day, 6.38% less than the week before. IDX's headline shows a rise of 114.64%. Regular-market value, where prices are set, was Rp46.78tn, down 0.77%. The same trades pulled the foreign share of trading down to 19%, against 37% the week before, because they ran from domestic seller to domestic buyer. Without them foreigners made about 44% of trading, more than the week before. One broker, Trimegah Sekuritas, handled 53.58% of member value for the week.

sections.title: Foreign buyers came back for three stocks

blocks.label: Exhibit 06
blocks.title: Net buying of Rp462.73bn, 95.83% of it on Thursday
blocks.note: Official all-market stock trading, foreign purchases less sales. This measures trading, not money leaving or entering the country.

blocks.text: Official foreign net buying was Rp462.73bn, after net selling of Rp167.11bn the week before. Thursday's Rp443.44bn was 95.83% of it. On Friday foreigners sold a net Rp229.77bn while the index rose 1.78%, so local buyers carried the last day. For 2026 as a whole foreign investors remain net sellers of Rp97.63tn.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 07. Estimated foreign net trading in selected liquid large caps, 9 to 13 November

blocks.text: Our estimate values IDX's daily foreign buy and sell shares at each day's close, across all markets. It sums to Rp618.98bn, Rp156.25bn more than the official net, so we use it to rank stocks and never as a total. Among 69 liquid large caps, worth Rp10tn or more with an average of Rp10bn or more of regular trading a day, three names took nearly all the buying. TLKM rose 9.09% while foreigners sold it. BRPT had the largest estimated selling, Rp119.27bn of it from Monday to Wednesday, before MSCI's review named it for removal.

sections.title: Five big stocks led, and IDX's tables mixed in the stocks that left

blocks.label: Exhibit 08
blocks.title: Five laggards and five leaders
blocks.note: Weekly IHSG points as IDX prints them on page 5. Our rebuild from index shares gives the same ten figures to within 0.01 point.

blocks.text: BBRI rose 8.90% and added 42.10 points. BBCA added 28.22, ASII 25.28, TLKM 20.83 and BMRI 18.93. Losses were small. BRPT was the largest drag at 3.02 points, and the ten largest drags together took 11.27 points by our count.

IDX's printed list of ten leaders has the right top five. Its other five, CDIA, GIAA, VICI, MLBI and UANG, added between 0.20 and 0.92 points each, and all five left the index on Friday. We rebuilt every stock's contribution from IDX's index shares and closes, and the rebuild matches each day's index change to within 0.001 point. On that count five staying stocks added more than any of them: BUMI 9.98 points, VKTR 9.07, BRMS 6.94, UNTR 6.90 and BBNI 5.51. The laggard list follows the same pattern. Its ten names are the five largest drags among the stocks that stay and the five largest among those that left, PANI, MAPI, NCKL, BDMN and BRIS. So IDX's tables read as the top five of each group put together, not as the ten largest movers. PANI and NCKL rose over the week yet show negative points, because only their fall up to Thursday counted.

blocks.label: Exhibit 09
blocks.title: Every sector rose, industrials and energy most
blocks.note: Weekly price changes of the IDX sector indices.

blocks.text: Industrials rose 9.55% and energy 9.49%. Healthcare barely moved, at 0.41%. Financials gained only 2.68% while the three largest banks rose 5.14% to 8.90%. IDX builds its sector indices differently from IHSG, and we could not rebuild them. Weighted the way IHSG weights its members, financial stocks rose 5.01%, and leaving out the ones IHSG dropped adds only 0.15 points. So the dropped stocks do not explain why the printed sector figure trailed. The Acceleration Board rose 12.56% and the Development Board 3.37%.

MSCI's November review came out on Thursday morning, Jakarta time. It removes BRPT and BRMS from MSCI's Standard index, moves BRMS to Small Cap and drops seven Indonesian names from Small Cap, RAJA among them. CNBC Indonesia and Kontan report the same list, and Kontan gives 1 December as the effective date. Prices give no clear reading of the list. RAJA rose 35.20% over the week, but it had gone from 392 to 520 before the list and closed at 530, and foreigners sold an estimated Rp50.32bn of it on Thursday. BRMS rose 9.43%, all of it on Friday.

sections.title: Why Thursday? The evidence is thin

rows: Relief after the vice president resigned
Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation that day, and CNBC Indonesia set it beside the rise
Kontan reported it as a source of political doubt and quotes an analyst saying that doubt raised the premium on Indonesian assets. The rupiah hit a record low the same day
Possible. The currency did not read it as relief
MSCI's review settled an open question
Published on Thursday morning, Jakarta time. CNBC Indonesia and Kontan both report it
No Indonesian stock was added to the Standard index. Bank Indonesia named worry about a possible MSCI downgrade as a pressure on the rupiah that morning
Over the week Taiwan rose 10.01%, the Nikkei 6.46% and the S&P 500 2.51%
On Thursday the Nikkei fell 0.70% and Kontan reports Taiwan down 2.6%
Explains the week better than the day
Official net buying of Rp443.44bn. BBRI took an estimated Rp506.79bn
This shows how prices rose, not why buyers came
Funds selling the stocks due to leave, after Wednesday evening's list
The 522 staying stocks rose 2.69% on Thursday and the 296 leaving ones 0.64%
IDX confirmed the leavers only after Thursday's close, and we have no figure for money that tracks IHSG
blocks.caption: Exhibit 10. Competing explanations for Thursday's 2.66% rise

blocks.text: We cannot name one cause. Thursday's rise was foreign buying of a few large banks on a day with two pieces of news, the MSCI review and the vice president's resignation, and neither clearly explains it. The rupiah's record low argues against reading it as a vote of confidence in Indonesia. Friday's 1.78% gain came with net foreign selling, and we found no dated source that explains it.

sections.title: Most of the world rose, and North Asia led

blocks.label: Exhibit 11
blocks.title: Indonesia was third of 32 markets in IDX's table
blocks.note: Changes from IDX's global table. Asian rows run Friday to Friday. IDX takes European and American markets at their last close before its report, so those rows run from Friday 6 November to Thursday 12 November. IDX lists the US only through the Dow, so the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rows use FRED closes for 6 and 13 November.

blocks.text: Taiwan rose 10.01% and Japan 6.46%, taking back much of the AI sell-off that hit them a week earlier. Korea gained 4.56%. Hong Kong fell 3.45%, the Philippines 2.92% and Malaysia 2.10%. Europe was firm, with Germany up 3.81% and the UK 2.03% from Friday to Thursday.

blocks.caption: Exhibit 12. US indices, FRED daily closes

blocks.text: In New York the S&P 500 rose 2.51% and the Nasdaq 100 3.53%, though both fell on Thursday and Friday. On 10 November the BLS reported October consumer prices up 0.4% in the month and 0.3% without food and energy. It could not publish a 12-month rate because October 2025 data were never collected. Treasury yields rose. By Thursday the two-year had gone from 4.51% to 4.86% and the ten-year from 4.86% to 5.10%.

sections.title: The rupiah paid for the rally

blocks.title: In dollars the week was about 5.31%
blocks.note: The starting values use this week's IHSG and BI JISDOR. Move the sliders to try a different currency assumption. The equity close and the reference rate are taken at different times.

blocks.text: JISDOR ended the week at 18,218, 0.49% weaker, after 18,241 on Thursday, its weakest reading since Bank Indonesia's series began in May 2013. The previous low was 18,183 on 28 October. CNBC Indonesia and Kontan both report a record low for the rupiah that day. Bank Indonesia's statement, as CNBC Indonesia reports it, blamed rising expectations of US rate increases in December and into 2027, along with worry about MSCI. It said it intervened in offshore and domestic forwards and in the spot market, and bought government bonds. Its board meets on 17 and 18 November.

Demand for government bonds came back. At Tuesday's auction investors bid Rp79.71tn, up from Rp31.09tn, and the government took Rp35tn. Bloomberg Technoz and Kontan both report those figures and FR0111's 7.67%. Bloomberg Technoz adds the Rp30tn target and the 7.55% at the previous sale. The price did not improve. FR0111, an 11-year bond, cleared at 7.67% against 7.55%. Lenders are back, and they want more to lend for long.

blocks.text: The downside test is a close below 5,027.964, this week's low and below last week's 5,050.429 close, which would undo the whole gain. With banks now a larger part of the index, foreign selling of BBRI and BMRI is the first thing we would watch.

sourceIntro: Checked on 15 November 2026 and again on 16 November. Market data end at the 13 November close. IDX statistics, IDX and KSEI announcements, IDX company filings, Bank Indonesia, FRED and the Bureau of Labor Statistics are primary sources. The main press facts rest on two outlets: CNBC Indonesia with Kontan for Thursday's market, the MSCI list and the rupiah, and Bloomberg Technoz with Kontan for the bond auction. Where only one outlet gives a detail, the text names it.

method: Weekly returns are computed from IDX closes. Breadth shares are recomputed from counts because IDX's printed percentages were misplaced. Index membership, counted free float and point contributions are rebuilt from IDX's stock summary and index shares, and the rebuild reproduces each day's index change. Turnover without the ADRO and AADI transfers subtracts their negotiated value on 10 November. Dollar returns use JISDOR. Stock-level foreign flows value IDX's foreign shares at the daily close and are not added to official totals.
